title: Renewal Prioritization — Flagship Accounts Portrait
content:
Purpose:
This is a working portrait for how we should prioritize renewals for flagship/strategic accounts heading into QBR season (Jan–Mar cadence). Focus is on combining classic tiering with deployment sensitivity and live usage telemetry to produce a single prioritization signal for outreach and executive prep.

High-level approach (tl;dr):
- Keep the tiers (Strategic / Enterprise / Scale / Starter) but treat them as a tie-breaker rather than the primary priority value.
- Create a Deployment Criticality multiplier: Private > Dedicated > Hosted (because network, SLA, and procurement timelines lengthen renewals).
- Blend ICP-fit, Recent Usage Trend, and Support Signal to compute a Renewal Priority Score (RPS).
- Surface a short list (top 20% by RPS, plus any expiring > $500k ARR) for executive touch and cross-functional war room.

Columns we should include in the sheet (ordered):
1) Account name
2) Tier (Strategic / Enterprise / Scale / Starter)
3) Net ARR (USD)
4) Renewal date
5) Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
6) Region (NA / EMEA / APAC / LATAM)
7) ICP fit (High / Medium / Low) — note short rationale: product-led, heavy customization, regulated sector, etc.
8) Recent usage trend (tokens per day / 30d delta) — normalized to 0–1
9) Support & reliability signals (open Sev1s past 90d, SLA incidents) — normalized to 0–1 (1 = many issues)
10) Adoption signals (active routes, models pinned, optimize features used) — 0–1
11) Procurement risk (Procurement lead in days, payment method complexity) — 0–1
12) Renewal Priority Score (computed)
13) Recommended QBR owner / AE / CSM
14) Suggested outreach cadence (Weekly / Biweekly / Monthly / Executive only)
15) Next playbook action (e.g., Exec intro + rollout plan, Technical deep-dive, Contract flexibility request, Win-back campaign)
16) Notes / unresolved blockers (legal terms, custom infra, pending POC)

Scoring rubric (make reproducible in sheet):
- Encode ICP fit: High=1.0, Medium=0.6, Low=0.2
- Tier weight: Strategic=1.0, Enterprise=0.8, Scale=0.5, Starter=0.2
- Deployment criticality multiplier: Private=1.25, Dedicated=1.1, Hosted=1.0
- Usage trend (norm): 0–1 where 1 = strong growth (>30% 30d) and 0 = steep decline
- Support signal penalty: subtract up to 0.25 from final score when support issues present

Renewal Priority Score (RPS) formula (sheet-friendly):
RPS = round( (0.45 * ICP_fit) + (0.25 * Tier_weight) + (0.20 * Usage_norm) + (0.10 * Adoption_signal), 3 ) * Deployment_multiplier - Support_penalty - Procurement_penalty
Examples (illustrative):
- Acme Corp (Strategic, High ICP, Private, usage up 40%, low support):
  ICP_fit=1.0, Tier=1.0, Usage=1.0, Adoption=0.9, Mult=1.25, Support_penalty=0 => RPS ≈ ((0.45+0.25+0.20+0.09)*1.25)=1.25 (capped at 1.25) => top priority
- BetaCo (Scale, Medium ICP, Hosted, usage down 15%, 1 Sev1 in 45d):
  ICP=0.6, Tier=0.5, Usage=0.2, Adoption=0.4, Mult=1.0, Support_penalty=0.15 => RPS ≈ 0.45*0.6 + 0.25*0.5 + 0.2*0.2 + 0.1*0.4 = 0.27+0.125+0.04+0.04=0.475 - 0.15 = 0.325 => mid-low

Priority buckets (post-RPS):
- Red (Immediate) — RPS >= 0.8 OR Net ARR >= $500k and renewal < 90d
- Amber (Monitor) — 0.5 <= RPS < 0.8
- Green (Standard) — RPS < 0.5

Playbook actions per bucket (short):
- Red: Executive sponsor outreach, legal + procurement kickoff, 2x-weekly syncs, technical readiness checklist, offer restricted price protection for 12 months
- Amber: Dedicated CSM touch, one technical QBR with optimization suggestions, SMS/email reminders 30/14/7 days pre-renewal, provisional canary of Dedicated if capacity shows need
- Green: Standard renewal flow, automated reminders, 60-day check-in only, upsell campaigns as applicable

Region & deployment notes (ops nuance):
- APAC private deployments often have longer procurement windows (avg 120d) — add +0.05 procurement_penalty to RPS unless procurement engaged.
- EMEA regs (data residency) increases risk for Hosted-only deployments — highlight legal blocker in Notes.
- Dedicated deployments frequently flag for capacity conversations; if utilization > 75% during renewal, escalate to capacity planning.

QBR prep checklist (for flagged accounts):
- One-pager for exec: topline ARR, last 12m delta, RPS justification, biggest blocker, ask (discount / technical resource / trial extension).
- Attach: 30d usage chart, SLA incidents summary, open backlog of feature requests, procurement timeline estimate.
- Pre-meeting: internal dry-run (30m) with AE + Eng TPM + CSM 72h before QBR.

Templates / Subject lines (quick):
- Exec outreach: "Redwood x <Account> — Quick renewal alignment (exec request)"
- Technical QBR invite: "<Account> — Technical QBR: performance, reliability, and plan"
- Finance/procurement: "Contract renewal timeline & procurement checklist — Redwood"

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need to finalize weights with Diego (are ICP weights too high versus tier weight?) — action: sync on 2026-03-12 (ticket JIRA-4237).
- Confirm how to pull normalized usage trend from telemetry dashboards (Priya to supply query).
- Decide whether to cap RPS at 1.2 to avoid runaway multipliers for Private deployments.
- Add boolean flag for multi-year deals (likely increases priority).

Operational notes for sheet owner (CS Ops):
- Build a calculated column for RPS (one formula cell that can be copied down). Keep normalization queries in hidden columns so coaches can audit.
- Create a pivot tab: top 50 by RPS, slice by region and deployment.
- Add conditional formatting: red/amber/green and a second heatmap for procurement lead time.

Example one-line playbook entries to paste into ABR/QBR slides:
- "Acme Corp — Flag: Private deploy, +40% 30d usage, renewal 45d. Action: Exec intro + procurement kickoff. Owner: Jonah."
- "BetaCo — Flag: Scale/usage down, 1 Sev1. Action: Technical deep-dive + reliability plan. Owner: Priya."

Closing notes (informal):
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — want something the CS Ops sheet can compute without too many manual judgments.
- The multiplier strategy puts weight on deployment friction which has been a recurring cause of late renewals.
- Happy to trim or reweight after one QBR cycle; comments below are welcome.

Comments (work-in-progress):
- Diego: "I think adoption_signal should be weighted equal to usage — otherwise we miss accounts using but not engaging features."
- Priya: "Procurement penalty needs to be region aware — I'm working up stats for APAC vs NA."

Unresolved: procurement dataset mapping to accounts (CS ops owns mapping)

End of draft.
